metadata.description: Canonical CS ontology entries for data structures taught in undergraduate CS courses.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A collection of elements of the same type stored in contiguous memory locations, accessible by index.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A linear data structure where elements (nodes) are stored in non-contiguous memory and linked via pointers.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A linked list where each node contains a pointer to both the next and the previous node.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A linear data structure following Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) order, supporting push and pop operations.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A linear data structure following First-In-First-Out (FIFO) order, supporting enqueue and dequeue operations.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: An abstract data type similar to a queue where each element has a priority and high-priority elements are served first.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A double-ended queue that supports insertion and deletion from both ends.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A data structure that maps keys to values using a hash function for average O(1) lookup.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A tree data structure in which each node has at most two children, referred to as left and right child.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A binary tree where each node's left subtree contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key, and right subtree only greater keys.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A self-balancing binary search tree where the heights of the two child subtrees differ by at most one.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A self-balancing binary search tree where each node has a colour (red or black) to ensure balanced height.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A self-balancing tree data structure that maintains sorted data and allows efficient insertions, deletions and lookups, widely used in databases.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A tree-like data structure used to store strings, where each node represents a common prefix.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A non-linear data structure consisting of vertices (nodes) and edges connecting them.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A complete binary tree where each parent node is greater (max-heap) or smaller (min-heap) than its children.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A heap where the parent node's key is always less than or equal to its children's keys.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A heap where the parent node's key is always greater than or equal to its children's keys.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A 2D matrix representation of a graph where cell [i][j] indicates an edge between vertex i and vertex j.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A collection of lists used to represent a graph, where each list contains the neighbours of a vertex.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A hierarchical non-linear data structure with a root node and subtrees of children, with no cycles.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A fundamental unit in linked lists, trees, and graphs that stores data and references to other nodes.

entries.label: DATA_STRUCTURE
entries.definition: A connection between two nodes in a graph or tree.
